messages:
Renee (People Ops): Heads up  compact update on two things we keep getting questions on: 1) the calibration scoring rubric (how to map evidence -> band) and 2) how comp sync interacts with ratings. Posting the short FAQ here so managers can paste into invites. Doc link: https://go/redwood/cal-rubric-compact :spiral_note_book:

Omar (People Ops): TL;DR rubric: evidence first, scope second, consistency third. Use 3 anonymized bullets + 1 recommended band in manager summary. Panels should cite evidence bullets when nudging band changes.

Felix (Eng Manager): Can you paste the rubric mapping? Managers want a quick copy-paste.

Renee (People Ops): Sure, paste this into manager guidance:

```
Rubric (one-line):
- Band 1 (Low): limited scope or recurring miss; evidence shows task-level impact only.
- Band 2 (Solid): reliable delivery on team goals; evidence shows consistent ownership.
- Band 3 (High): multiplatform/strong cross-team impact or large scope; evidence shows measurable org impact.
- Band 4 (Exceptional): sustained, outsized outcomes + strategic influence outside org.
```

Add metrics where possible (KPIs, % change, incidents resolved). Avoid naming individuals in evidence.

June (IC): For cross-functional ICs who support multiple teams, how does scope get judged? I feel scope is fuzzy.

Omar (People Ops): Good point. Panels weight direct measurable impact higher than claimed scope. If you have cross-team PRs, link 1-2 artifacts in the manager summary (PRs, dashboards, postmortems). Panels will consider artifacts as evidence to validate scope.

Asha (Finance): Quick comp note: we don't use the manager's initial recommended comp number during calibration. Compensation alignment happens after ratings lock in a separate worksheet where Finance & People Ops map bands -> comp ranges. Please don't include comp asks in the manager summary.

Felix (Eng Manager): If panel changes the band, does compensation always change? Managers ask this often.

Renee (People Ops): Not always. Ratings and comp are correlated but distinct. Panel can adjust a band based on evidence; Finance then maps final band to comp guidance. If there's a large pay gap, Recruiting/Finance may ask for an exception. We try to keep these as separate steps to reduce bias.

NotifyBot: Reminder: manager summaries due in 5 days. Upload: https://go/redwood/manager-upload :bell:

June (IC): Is there an appeals timeline? If I disagree with the final rating, what now?

Omar (People Ops): Appeals window is 10 business days post-release. Appeals should include new evidence or process concerns and go to People Ops for triage. We aim to resolve escalations within 7 business days of appeal submission.

Felix (Eng Manager): One more request  can People Ops add a 2-slide calibration training (5 min) I can paste in manager invites? Some of my peers skip the workshop.

Renee (People Ops): Yes. I'll upload a 2-slide "Evidence-first calibration" deck and a 5-min recording to the anchors doc. Link will be in the main cycle doc by EOD. Use it in invites for panelists.

Asha (Finance): Also ping Finance early if you have any pending offers or comp-sensitive cases during the window. Helps us avoid rework after ratings.

Renee (People Ops): Thanks all  will follow up with the paste-ready snippets and the 2-slide deck. DM me for edge cases (LOA, international comp cycles).
